chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Origin of the piano-and-drums act and the San Francisco earthquake
summary: Johnny was a saloon pianist; after the 1906 earthquake, where Reb led him to his operation, he got the idea of adding drums, which made them a sensation in Arizona.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Uh, when you said that Johnny came back into town...uh, somewhere around 1907 or so, uh, where had he been travelling, and whom had he been working with on the road?
Well, he was just a piano player then, see? He didn't have a musical act. We formed the act. See, when he took me with him, then we built into the act, but before that, he was a

trumpet and piano player but mostly piano, see, and in those days, a Negro couldn't play nowhere but in a sportin' house or the back end of a saloon. That's the only place most of the piano players played, and that's where he played. In saloons, those days, they had a piano sittin' up on the bandstand. You a piano player come in and play while the other guys playin' poker and things around. And so when he come home, he says, "I'm gonna take you with me," and he bought me a set of drums, and he taught me a little about how to hit, you know, to play the drums and things, and we were a sensation in Arizona 'cause they hadn't heard of that, and a lot of places would hire me...would want me but wouldn't want him but they would have to take the team. They wanted a drummer. They'd never...all the dancers and things, all in Bisbee and Douglas, Arizona, like that. The Germans would get drunk, and the Spanish and everything. We'd be the music --piano and drums.
So you played dances, and then the places you told me, like the mining camps, the theaters. Uh huh.

Yeah. It was quite a novelty--piano and drums. And it was so...and where we got the idea was, during the earthquake in San Francisco, you know, when I went up there with my other brother, and that's where he came blind, and I used to have to take him every day out to the...out to have his operation. We'd walk 'cause there was no streetcars, and the streets was all full of bricks and stones and old buildings and things, and I'd have to walk him from Montgomery Street clear out...I don't know what the name of that street is now

out there--a mile...a mile-and-a-half, and we'd walk back, and he'd... for his operation in San Francisco. And all the dancehalls up there then had drums and piano, you see, so that's where he got the idea, then he bought me some drums, and when we went to Arizona, playing around, everybody wanted the drums and piano. Every dance in town almost they had was...we'd be playing.
